title: cross-session-data-stitching-and-fallbacks-wip
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working note capturing an operator-first approach for handling cross-session (multi-request, short-lived) user interactions when region pinning prevents direct data access in the preferred region. Focus is on: (1) how to reliably stitch ephemeral session state when parts of state live in a pinned region, (2) fallback behaviors when pinned region is unreachable or constrained, and (3) telemetry and rollback criteria for canarying these behaviors for customers using soft or conditional pinning.

Background / Problem statement:
- Some customers use pinning to anchor tenant data to region X. Many application flows rely on session-scoped artifacts (prefix cache, KV blobs, short-lived embeddings) that are created in the initial request and referenced by subsequent requests.
- Under normal operation these artifacts are colocated in the pinned region. However, for high availability we sometimes need to serve subsequent requests from failover regions (due to outages, regional capacity limits, or cross-region latency routing).
- Without a stitch/fallback strategy, apps see missing context, failed inference chains, or hidden data exfil risks (if we naïvely replicate ephemeral state across regions).

Goals and constraints:
- Preserve strong residency guarantees for long-lived tenant data and keys. Do not replicate permanent customer data across region boundaries by default.
- Allow read-only or degraded session continuation when safe, with clear audit evidence showing whether session state was reconstructed or proxied.
- Minimize latency impact: primary preference is to proxy metadata/kv reads to pinned region when latency budget allows; otherwise use tiered fallback with operator-visible signals.
- Provide operators and sales with deterministic customer-visible behaviors and templates for comms and SLAs.

Key concepts / terminology:
- Sticky prefix: prefix cache items created during initial requests and referenced later in the same logical session. Typically TTLed (seconds–minutes).
- Session anchor: the authoritative pointer (region, shard, object id) that indicates where authoritative session artifacts are stored for a tenant.
- Stitch proxy: short-lived proxy path that forwards read-only session artifact lookups to the anchor region.
- Ephemeral replication: selective, time-limited replication of session artifacts to a failover region with strict erasure/TTL and audit trace.

Proposed operator flows (high level):
1) Normal: client -> routing policy -> pinned region -> session artifacts read locally. No special behavior.
2) Proxy fallback (preferred when latency < 250ms extra): client -> failover region -> detect session anchor points -> async proxy read to pinned region (X-Res-Proxy: true) -> return response with header indicating proxied reads.
3) Degraded local replay: if proxy exceeds latency budget or pinned region denies (rate-limit/outage), attempt local best-effort replay using latest cached deltas. Insert deterministic string marker in output and emit telemetry.
4) Ephemeral replication (last resort, operator-controlled): replicate limited artifacts (only non-PII, hashed KV) with TTL <= 5m and write audit record. Use this only if customer opted-in (contractual) or during automated grace for critical latency SLOs.

Telemetry and signals to emit (minimum):
- residency.session_anchor_hit: boolean (true when request served from anchor region)
- residency.proxy_read_latency_ms: histogram
- residency.fallback_mode: enum(proxy, local-replay, ephemeral-rep)
- residency.replicated_keys_count: count
- residency.audit_evidence_id: correlation id for later audit extraction

Acceptance criteria for canary (metrics to watch):
- <= 0.5% of requests for canary tenants use ephemeral replication during 72h canary window.
- Successful proxy read rate > 98% when pinned region is up but behind high latency windows.
- No PII replication incidents in logs (automated scan).
- Operator rollback trigger: if error-rate increases by >3x or customer-facing latency p95 degrades >100ms for canary tenants.

Operator runbook (quick):
- Detect: residency.fallback_mode != null at scale in production -> open ticket, tag oncall.
- Mitigate: toggle proxy-read-timeout config (runtime flag) to a stricter value; scale pinned region read-tails if overloaded.
- Rollback: disable ephemeral replication toggle and purge any ephemeral stores with audit_evidence_id tag. Notify legal & compliance if any TTL exceeded.

Testing / simulation plan (stubs):
- Synthetic session generator: create chained 5-request session, vary initial anchor creation in region A, then route subsequent requests to region B. Verify headers, audit ids, and outcome.
- Chaos test: introduce 500ms added latency between B and pinned region for 10m during a canary. Measure proxy latencies and fallback rate.
- Privacy scan: fuzz test ephemeral replication payloads to ensure no un-hashed PII.

Customer communication templates (short):
- Status update snippet (for support): "We served your session in a degraded mode while region X experienced capacity constraints. No permanent customer data was replicated. We have trace id: <audit_evidence_id> for troubleshooting."
- Opt-in consent blurb (UI): "Allow temporary, encrypted session replication to alternate regions to improve availability for short sessions (expires automatically)."

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default policy for proxies: should we proxy reads for all soft-pinned tenants or only enterprise customers? (Security tradeoffs)
- How to cryptographically prove to auditors that ephemeral replication did not persist beyond TTL? (suggestion: HSM-signed ephemeral manifests)
- Operator ergonomics: what UI/flags in Console should be visible for toggling ephemeral replication per-tenant?

Next steps / action items:
- (Priya) Draft minimal telemetry dashboard and add residency.* metrics to SLO board (due 2026-02-28).
- (Ethan) Implement simple proxy-read header and perf test harness (ENG-9123) — draft PR 486 needs review.
- (Mariana) Draft legal-safe language for opt-in and ephemeral replication guarantees; sync with Legal on audit evidence format.
- (Jared) Set up chaos experiment and schedule 2h canary run for selected internal tenants.

References / links: see linked_artifacts above.

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally operational — will prune into a formal runbook after 2 successful canary windows. Still rough — many TODOs.
